about: Shared scoring spec for the MCP server (openbionews/mcp_server.py) and the website (docs/index.html). tests/test_ranking_parity.py feeds every case to BOTH implementations and checks each against `expected`, so the two can't drift apart. Change a weight on purpose -> update the expected values here, and both implementations must follow.

trial_salience.formula: mean(enrollment, phase, results_posted, maturity); enrollment = min(1, log10(n+1)/log10(5001)); phase = max over listed phases

cases.name: combined Phase 2/3 takes the higher weight
no phase, no enrollment, unknown status

generic_salience.formula: with a source signal: 0.6*signal + 0.3*recency + 0.1*match; without: 0.6*recency + 0.4*match. recency = max(0, 1 - whole_days_old/365)

cases.name: Class II recall, over a year old
Class I recall with a full query match
Federal Register notice over a year old

known_divergences: Approvals signal: the MCP server scores priority review (1.0 vs 0.5) from openFDA's submission data; the website scores original approval vs supplement (1.0 vs 0.6) from its card title. Different inputs, so approvals are not in these cases.

Relevance mode (rank_by=relevance / the website's Update mode): the MCP server measures match as the share of query terms a record contains; the website uses BM25 normalised across the records on the page. Only the salience blends are pinned here.
